# Problem statement — <product name>

Status: Draft | In review | Approved
Author(s): <owner / agent> · Date: YYYY-MM-DD · Process log: <link>

## 1. The problem

*One paragraph. Who has it, when it occurs, what it costs them. No solution
words ("app", "dashboard", "AI") in this section.*

## 2. Who we are building for

*Primary user and, if any, secondary users. What they already do today to
cope. What they would never tolerate.*

## 3. Why now / why this

*What makes this worth doing at this moment: a learning goal, a portfolio
goal, a market gap, a technology that just became viable. Be honest — a
portfolio goal is a legitimate "why".*

## 4. What success looks like

*Observable outcomes, not features. For a portfolio: what a reviewer should
be able to conclude in ten minutes. For a product: what the user can do that
they could not before. 3–5 bullets, each checkable.*

## 5. Constraints

*Time, budget, licences (e.g. design file may not be published), skills to
demonstrate, technologies deliberately in or out.*

## 6. Out of scope

*What we are explicitly not doing, so nobody has to ask.*

## 7. Assumptions

*Things we believe without proof. Each gets a row in
`assumptions-and-questions.md`.*

## 8. Open questions

*What we need to learn before requirements can be written. Each has an owner
and a "must be answered by" phase.*
